editorial:
Imagine living in a house where the shadows actually move and something mean is hiding in your closet. You follow a teenage girl and her little sister who are already sad because they lost their mom. To make things worse, their dad is so heartbroken that he barely notices when things start going wrong. It feels like a heavy, scary mood from the start, and you can really feel the stress of the kids trying to warn their father about the monster before it catches them. It is a creepy ride that plays on those childhood fears we all had about the dark.

The acting is solid, especially with the kids, and the jump scares are timed well to keep you on edge. While the plot is a bit simple and some parts move a little slow, the monster design is genuinely spooky. If you love supernatural scares, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The family discovers that the monster feeds on grief and sadness. In the final showdown, the father finally wakes up and helps his daughters fight back. They realize they have to stop being sad and start fighting together to defeat the creature. They manage to trap the Boogeyman and kill it, finally breaking the cycle of pain. The movie ends with the family healing and finding peace now that the monster is gone for good.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves monster movies and jump scares.
